name: Dysostosis with combined reduction defects of upper and lower limbs

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and radiological criteria for dysostosis with combined limb reduction defects

criteria.description: Presence of combined reduction defects affecting both upper and lower limbs
Radiographic evidence of dysostosis including abnormal bone formation and segmentation
Exclusion of other syndromic causes of limb reduction defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of combined limb reduction defects with characteristic radiological dysostosis and exclusion of other syndromes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not always definitive due to heterogeneity.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Combined transverse and longitudinal limb reduction defects
searchTerms: missing parts of limbs across and along length
combined limb shortening and missing segments

pathognomonic.symptomName: Segmental bone hypoplasia in upper and lower limbs
searchTerms: underdeveloped bone segments in arms and legs
partial bone growth defects in limbs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Radiographic evidence of dysostosis with abnormal ossification centers
searchTerms: X-rays show abnormal bone growth centers
short long bones in arms or legs
stiff joints in arms or legs
missing or very small fingers or toes

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in affected joints

occasional.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones due to limb defects
searchTerms: slow development of movement skills due to limb problems
delayed motor milestones from limb defects

rare.symptomName: Respiratory compromise secondary to thoracic deformities
searchTerms: respiratory issues caused by thoracic abnormalities

laboratory: Genetic testing may reveal mutations in genes associated with limb development
imaging: X-rays showing combined transverse and longitudinal limb reduction defects
Abnormal ossification centers and bone segmentation abnormalities
Possible thoracic cage deformities on chest imaging
genetic: Mutations in genes regulating limb patterning and bone formation (specific genes may vary)
Often sporadic but familial cases reported
other: Prenatal ultrasound may detect limb reduction defects
Physical examination revealing limb shortening and digit anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Absent radius with normal lower limbs
Synostosis of humerus, radius, and ulna

redFlags: Severe limb reduction defects incompatible with functional ambulation
Respiratory distress due to thoracic cage abnormalities
Presence of cardiac malformations requiring urgent intervention
references: Orphanet: Dysostosis with combined reduction defects of upper and lower limbs - ORPHA:294957
Rosenberg HK, et al. Limb reduction defects: clinical and genetic aspects. Am J Med Genet A. 2020.
